text:
R305 — Linux replica CPU-affinity and memory-admission port contract
Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: read-only review of official pristine v0.1.43 source at supplied HEAD 7695859 and immutable curated source at task-supplied HEAD 840db05 in perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012. Reviewed official serve/cpu_affinity.py, replicas.py, server.py, setup.py and curated launcher/config/host-memory logic. Also consulted R302 only for prior scope and official Python/Linux documentation. No active implementation worktree was read. No test/import/build/GPU/service/Git/cleanup/temp-file operation was performed.

Decision

If data-parallel replicas are ported to Linux SYCL, keep the feature opt-in and all-or-nothing. Compute each child’s CPU mask only from the server’s effective allowed CPUs, keep SMT siblings of each physical core in one replica, and apply the mask in a child launcher before exec. Do not execute Python preexec_fn from the threaded server. Before launching any child, estimate aggregate per-process model memory against the tighter of host available RAM and applicable cgroup memory headroom; the current one-engine warnings do not admit N independent model processes. Resolve every selected GPU group from stable PCI BDF identity at each start and verify the index mapping before spawning. A single Intel Arc B570 is one physical GPU and cannot form two disjoint GPU groups; GPU-free fixtures can qualify parsing, partitioning, resource arithmetic and rollback, but cannot qualify actual SYCL device selection or hardware behavior.

Source findings

The official replica bundle is opt-in. setup.py saves a replica count only when selected GPU indices divide evenly; it warns when os.cpu_count() is below 8 times the replica count but this is a host CPU-count warning, not an effective cpuset or memory admission. serve/replicas.py validates disjoint index groups and partitions CPUs. cpu_affinity.py groups only allowed logical CPUs by physical_package_id/core_id, keeps available SMT siblings of a core together, and divides physical cores across instances. The server currently applies the mask using Popen(preexec_fn=lambda: os.sched_setaffinity(0, cpus)). Replicas normally start concurrently in Python threads; STRATA_REPLICA_START=serial selects sequential construction. If any replica constructor fails, the server closes constructed engines and raises a startup error.

The official memory checks are advisory and single-instance shaped. setup model RAM/context recommendations are computed for one model process. server.warn_budget_over_ram inspects only the first replica’s args and warns against one resident budget using psutil host total/available. warn_tight_ram compares one engine’s arena_mib with host total and a 6 GiB remainder. These are warnings, not admission refusals, and do not multiply independent engine memory by replica count or account for cgroup limits. The setup check os.cpu_count() likewise does not represent the launcher’s allowed CPU set.

The curated baseline has no replica or affinity implementation. Its one-engine launcher config stores the primary Intel GPU as gpu_pci and extra layer-split devices as split_pci. setup enumerates Intel xe/i915 devices in PCI order and assigns index values; it later resolves saved PCI IDs to current indices. The server passes the primary PCI address through STRATA_GPU_PCI. This is a single engine’s layer-split selection, not data-parallel replicas. Treat R302’s prior replica/affinity omission as context only; this report addresses safe adaptation conditions, not that feature audit. R303’s watchdog is unrelated and is not repeated.

Thread-safe child affinity

Python’s subprocess documentation explicitly warns that preexec_fn is unsafe in threaded applications because the child can deadlock before exec. The replica server already creates engine launch threads, and the server also runs request/telemetry threads. Do not port the current preexec_fn lambda as-is.

Use one of these child-only routes:

- Launch a resolved taskset executable with an argv list, for example [taskset, "--cpu-list", "2,3,6,7", absolute_engine_path, "--serve", ...]. Do not use shell=True or interpolate a shell command. Pass cwd, env, stdin/stdout/stderr and text settings through Popen unchanged. Confirm taskset exists before enabling affinity; if absent, either use the helper below or disable affinity with an explicit warning.
- Preferably use a tiny standalone launcher process that receives a validated integer mask, calls os.sched_setaffinity(0, mask), verifies its own effective mask, then calls os.execvpe(engine, argv, env). Spawn that launcher normally from Popen with no preexec_fn; it has no application threads or inherited Python locks. Keep it independent of importing the server package. Exec preserves the launched process identity and standard streams while replacing the helper image with the engine.

In either case, never call sched_setaffinity(0, mask) in the parent server: Python/Linux define pid 0 as the calling thread for affinity reads and writes, and changing it there could pin the server thread instead of only the engine. After engine start and READY, verify the process and worker-thread masks are subsets of the assigned child mask and the server’s affinity is unchanged. If the requested mask is rejected or altered, do not claim isolation; report the actual mask or disable the affinity feature.

Mask construction contract

1. Read the effective allowed logical CPUs using sched_getaffinity(0) from the launcher’s calling thread, not os.cpu_count(). The current allowed set should already reflect scheduler/cpuset constraints; when available, compare it with cgroup cpuset.cpus.effective. Do not widen the mask to online CPUs or add an SMT sibling outside the allowed set.
2. Read package/core topology for every allowed CPU. Partition only those allowed CPUs; assign all allowed siblings of one physical core to the same replica, so two replicas do not each receive half of one physical core. If topology is missing/invalid or the allowed mask changes during construction, fail the affinity plan or explicitly run without isolation; never guess topology or silently widen the mask.
3. Require at least one distinct allowed physical core per replica. Reserve cores for the server/OS only by subtracting them from the allowed set before partitioning; record that policy. Upstream uses all allowed cores and does not reserve a separate server core, so the server may still compete on cores assigned to engines. If a strict minimum core count or reserved set is unsatisfied, reject affinity partitioning or visibly select the unpinned shared-core mode; do not report pinned replicas.
4. Keep the assigned sets pairwise disjoint, nonempty, and subsets of the effective allowed set. Preserve SMT siblings together where all are allowed; use only the allowed siblings where the cpuset exposes a subset.
5. Treat cgroup CPU quota separately from the cpuset mask. A quota can constrain runtime even when many CPUs appear in the allowed set; it is not permission to add CPUs or evidence that enough physical cores are reserved.

GPU identity and group mapping

Persist each replica’s selected GPU group as PCI BDF identities, not only enumeration indices. At launch, enumerate the current devices, build a unique BDF-to-index map, resolve each configured BDF, and fail before any child starts if an ID is absent, duplicated, unsupported, or maps ambiguously. Derive the engine’s indices and STRATA_GPU_PCI/split-device settings from that one checked map, then verify each child’s effective reported BDF/device at startup. Device indices can change with enumeration; BDF is the stable join key across setup, telemetry and runtime identity. Do not identify devices by marketing name or device ID alone.

Replica groups must be nonempty, pairwise disjoint, and collectively match the intended selected cards. A one-card B570 configuration cannot satisfy two independent GPU replica groups. Do not duplicate the B570 BDF in two groups or treat a multi-GPU layer split as independent replicas. On the current single-B570 host, actual replica startup/device mapping remains untestable and is not qualified here.

Aggregate memory admission

A safe preflight must consider the full set of N engine processes before the first spawn. Estimate each engine’s private resident experts/arena, dense model and runtime buffers, context KV, prefill/workspace, worker/pinned buffers and per-process runtime overhead; include one server/API overhead and the required system headroom. Model/context estimates from setup describe one instance and cannot be used unchanged for N independent copies. For mmap-backed weights, count sharing only when the exact mapping/sharing behavior is established; do not assume the OS page cache or expert residency is free. Serial startup can lower transient loading pressure but does not lower steady-state N-process memory.

Use a conservative available-memory ceiling: host MemAvailable and every finite applicable cgroup ancestor limit minus current charged usage; the lowest remaining limit governs. cgroup v2 memory.current accounts the cgroup and descendants, and memory.max is its hard limit. A missing/inaccessible limit is unknown rather than unlimited. Include a safety margin and concurrent startup peak; account for model loading overshoot and ordinary service/desktop usage. If the estimate or effective limit is unavailable, do not auto-admit replicas silently: remain single-engine or require an explicit operator choice with a clear risk statement. If predicted aggregate need plus margin exceeds the available ceiling, refuse prelaunch before any process is created. An opt-in override may bypass the estimate only if the product explicitly supports that risk; it must not be the default.

The rollback path must be all-or-nothing: record each child handle as soon as it is launched, including the child whose constructor later fails during READY or INFO parsing. On any partial failure, stop and reap every launched child, join every launch thread, and only then return the original startup error. Preserve cleanup errors as additional diagnostics without hiding the first failure. Do not return a Router/ReplicaEngine with fewer children than configured. If cleanup cannot reap a child, report its identity and retain the failed startup state rather than silently continuing.

GPU-free fake fixture contract

These are proposed deterministic host-only fixtures, not tests run in this audit:

- Affinity partition: fake sched_getaffinity returns a constrained set such as {2,3,6,7} while fake os.cpu_count reports a much larger host count. Mock sysfs package/core topology with SMT siblings and verify pairwise-disjoint groups, siblings in the same group, exact subset of allowed CPUs, no widening, and rejection when physical-core count is below replica count.
- Cpuset and topology edges: allowed set contains one sibling but not its partner; fake topology files missing, unreadable, malformed or hotplugged between plan and spawn. Verify the implementation never adds the disallowed sibling and never falsely claims partition success.
- Parent/child behavior: fake launcher argv for each replica, assert no preexec_fn/shell, parent affinity unchanged, the child receives exactly its planned mask before exec, engine argv/env/streams survive exec, and the post-READY effective mask matches the child group.
- PCI mapping: reorder fake GPU enumeration while keeping BDFs stable; confirm each replica still maps to its intended BDF and derived runtime index. Test absent/duplicate BDF, index collision, unsupported device, duplicate group membership, missing B570, and a one-B570/two-replica request; each fails before launch.
- Memory admission: fake host MemAvailable and cgroup ancestor memory.current/memory.max values; verify the tightest ceiling, one global headroom plus per-engine private estimates, N-fold private resident/arena costs, model/context growth, safe refusal above limit, unknown-limit behavior, and that serial launch changes transient estimate only—not steady-state admission. Inject malformed/negative/inconsistent counters and exceptions; never treat them as unlimited memory.
- Partial start failure: a fake launcher/engine factory marks each child started, then injects one replica READY failure while peers start normally. Verify every launched child is stopped/reaped, threads joined, first error retained, cleanup errors preserved, and no engine/router is published. Repeat with failure before handle registration to prove the launcher interface registers handles before the risky startup/readiness phase.
- No GPU assertion: these fixtures do not prove the Arc B570 can load two independent engines, that GPU memory fits, that Level Zero selects the intended PCI device, or that concurrent SYCL runtimes are safe. Those need an actual multi-device host and serialized, separately authorized device validation.

Evidence and references

- Official v0.1.43 source (supplied commit 7695859): serve/cpu_affinity.py partitioning; serve/replicas.py group validation, cpu_sets and child config; serve/server.py preexec_fn, concurrent/serial startup and partial cleanup; setup.py replica count/core warning.
- Curated source (task-supplied commit 840db05): setup.py gpus() PCI-order indices and saved gpu_pci/split_pci; server.py one-engine child_env, layer split, host RAM warnings; no replica startup path. R302 records the prior server-feature distinction.
- Python documentation: subprocess warns that preexec_fn can deadlock in threaded applications: [subprocess.Popen](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.Popen). Affinity methods and pid-zero calling-thread semantics: [os.sched_setaffinity](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.sched_setaffinity).
- Linux kernel documentation: cpuset.cpus.effective describes CPUs actually granted: [cgroup v2 cpuset interface](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html#cpuset-interface-files); memory.current and memory.max describe current cgroup charge and hard limit: [cgroup v2 memory interface](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html#memory-interface-files).
- R302 was read for existing scope only; its earlier 3141c18 baseline and replica-import finding are not re-audited here. R303 watchdog safety is unrelated and not repeated.

No runtime or performance claim is made. The B570 one-GPU host cannot validate independent multi-GPU replicas; CPU-only fake fixtures can validate only the host-side contracts above.
